new_statements.rule_in_words: Dynamic (expiratory) stress, fixed on the final syllable of the (suffixed) word/stem in native Nogai words; the hedge 'как правило' (as a rule) signals exceptions that the source does not enumerate.
new_statements.exceptions: None enumerated; 'как правило' implies exceptions. The Tatar Wikipedia summary (tertiary, citing this longread) adds that stress can serve to distinguish homonyms, which is not in Bulgarova's text.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('корней и основ' = roots and stems, i.e. the suffixed word); nothing on phrase-level accent or citation forms. The source is an expert-authored popular-science sketch by a Nogai linguist, not a reference grammar; it does not cite a source for the stress sentence.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement concerns the Nogai literary language as a whole (noga1249); no dialect (Karanogai / Aknogai / Nogai proper) is singled out. The Astrakhan varieties (Karagash, Alabugat, Yurt Tatar) that Glottolog lists under noga1249's descriptive refs (Arslanov 1992, 1997) were not reached.

new_statements.quote: В ногайском языке ударение экспираторное, фиксированное и, как правило, падает на последний слог ногайских корней и основ. Исключением являются слова, которые произносятся с особой интонацией, логически выделяющей эти слова. К этой группе исключений относятся: а) количественные числительные с интонацией перечисления, напр.: эки 'два'; алты 'шесть'; ети 'семь'; б) форма повелительного наклонения второго лица с интонацией повеления или приказа, напр.: олтыр! 'садись!'; в) вопросительные местоимения с интонацией вопроса, напр.: кайсы? 'который?'. Исключением являются также слова, к которым присоединяются следующие безударные аффиксы: а) аффиксы отрицательной формы глагола ...
new_statements.translation: In Nogai, stress is expiratory, fixed and, as a rule, falls on the last syllable of Nogai roots and stems. Exceptions are words pronounced with a special intonation that logically singles them out: (a) cardinal numerals with enumerating intonation, e.g. eki 'two', alty 'six', eti 'seven'; (b) the 2nd-person imperative with an intonation of command, e.g. oltyr! 'sit down!'; (c) interrogative pronouns with question intonation, e.g. kajsy? 'which?'. Also exceptions are words taking the following unstressed affixes: (a) verbal negation affixes, e.g. alma 'do not take' ... [continues: (b) person affixes in conjugated verb forms, alaman 'I take'; (c) the similative affix, baladaj 'like a child'; (d) the adverb-forming affix, russha 'in Russian'].
new_statements.citation: Baskakov, N. A. (ed.) 1963. Nogajsko-russkij slovar' s priloženiem grammatičeskogo očerka nogajskogo jazyka. Moscow: GIS. (grammar sketch, pp. 495–562)

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement and type as the catalog record (Bulgarova 2020, Postnauka): her sentence «Ударение в ногайском языке экспираторное, фиксированное и, как правило, падает на последний слог ногайских корней и основ» is Baskakov 1963 p. 507 nearly verbatim, so the catalog statement now has its primary printed source; Baskakov adds the exception classes (intonationally marked numerals/imperatives/interrogatives) and the list of unstressed affixes (negation, person endings, -дай, -ша), plus the musical phrase-stress remark.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is dynamic (expiratory), fixed, and as a rule on the last syllable of the root/stem, i.e. word-final as stressable suffixes are added; it is not final in (i) words spoken with a special 'logical' intonation — cardinal numerals in counting, 2nd-person imperatives, interrogative pronouns (examples printed with the accent on the first syllable: э́ки, а́лты, о́лтыр!, ка́йсы?) — and (ii) words carrying unstressed affixes: verbal negation -ма (а́лма, алма́дым), person endings of finite verbs (ала́ман, алга́нман), similative -дай (бала́дай, а́ттай), adverbial -ша (ру́сша, мени́мше), where stress stays on the syllable before the affix. Phrase stress is described as musical/tonic (intonation contours). On p. 505 narrow vowels are unreduced 'in the last syllable with strong stress' (арык, билим) and reduced 'in an unstressed syllable or a syllable with weak stress' (first syllables of кызыл, тилек).
new_statements.secondary_stress: no explicit secondary-stress rule; p. 505 speaks of syllables 'with weak stress' (со слабым ударением) versus the final syllable 'with strong stress', without locating the weak stress
new_statements.exceptions: non-final stress with emphatic/logical intonation: cardinal numerals (enumeration), 2sg imperative, interrogative pronouns; unstressed (pre-stressing) affixes: verbal negative -ма/-ме, personal endings of conjugated verb forms, similative -дай/-дей, adverb-forming -ша/-ше; Russian loans keep non-Nogai syllable types (p. 507) and lack palatal harmony (p. 505) but no separate loan-stress rule is stated in this section
new_statements.identity_note: Standard literary Nogai as codified in the 1963 dictionary (Karachay-Cherkess Research Institute; Baskakov's sketch covers the literary language based on the three dialects — собственно ногайский, караногайский, акногайский — described in its introduction); not the Astrakhan/Yurt/Alabugat varieties.
